title: Book Three · Chapter 201: Eight Hours to the Coast
story:
At a quarter past six on Sunday, Ronan lifts the travel bag from beside the green door.

Dad takes one handle while they walk. Mum carries the smaller cloth bag for the first part of the road.

They reach the station around twenty to seven. The bus is waiting, and the driver checks Ronan's ticket.

Dad puts the large bag in the luggage space. Mum gives Ronan his cloth bag and straightens its strap.

For a moment, he looks from one face to the other.

“I will write when I am there.”

“Tell us the ordinary things,” Mum says.

Dad takes his shoulder, then lets his hand fall.

“Find the office first.”

Ronan smiles and nods. He holds Mum close, then Dad. Afterward, he steps onto the bus with the small bag beside him.

Through the window, he can see both parents near the waiting space. He lifts his hand. They lift theirs.

At seven, the bus leaves.

Ronan watches the station turn out of sight. Then the market road goes past, followed by streets he knows less well.

He keeps the ticket in his cloth case. The blue cord is still around his wrist.

For a while, he watches the road. Later, he opens his phrase book at the visitor page.

“I would like a room,” he reads quietly.

The man beside him smiles toward the window.

“After this seat, so would I.”

Ronan laughs softly and closes the book for a rest.

The bus slows at a bend. Ronan's small bag slides against his leg. He catches it and puts it between his feet.

“Your books?” the man asks.

“Yes.”

“Far to carry a library.”

“Only a small one.”

Ronan smiles at the familiar joke. He puts one hand on the top of the bag. At home, Dad could ask him to bring a book from the shelf. Here, the shelf is far behind him.

The man turns back to the window. Ronan looks out too. He cannot name the streets now. At each stop, he listens to the driver before he relaxes again.

After a while, he takes out the route sheet. The words for the coastal station are clear. The next part begins outside its entrance.

He folds the sheet along the old lines and puts it where he can reach it. Then he opens the food Mum packed. The cloth bag stays between his shoes while he eats.

He eats some bread and fruit during the journey. His water bottle is still half full after lunch.

Early in the afternoon, he sees water beyond the buildings. At first, there is only a long blue line. Then the road turns, and the open sea comes into view.

Ronan leans toward the glass. The water goes much farther than the river at home.

He stays there until another row of buildings hides it again.

At three, after eight hours on the road, the bus reaches the coastal station.

Ronan checks the stop with the driver. He waits for the other passengers, then carries his cloth bag down the steps.

Outside, he collects the large travel bag. It is heavier now that he must carry it alone.

He puts both bags beside his feet and takes out the centre's route sheet. The main journey is finished. The local bus stop is just beyond the station entrance, and he turns toward it with the paper in his hand.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

luggage space＝放大件行李的位置；passenger＝乘客；come into view＝出现在眼前；coast＝海岸。

## 理解问题

1. 他几点离家、到站、发车及到沿海？是否真正走完约八小时主程？
2. 随身哪些旧物仍在？到达主站后还剩哪一段实际路程？

## 读句子

**At seven, the bus leaves.**

拆开看：At seven, / the bus / leaves.

七点／大巴／实际出发。
